public_payload.normalized_proposition: The vast, vast majority of AI compute demand comes from services provided either free or at such a massive discount that it is impossible that anyone on a $20 or $200-a-month plan could afford them at their actual token cost.

statement.excerpt: The vast, vast majority of AI compute demand is from services provided to people either for free or sold at such a massive discount that it’s impossible that anyone on a $20 or $200-a-month plan could even afford these services had they paid their actual token cost.

from_speaker: The vast, vast majority of AI compute demand
services provided to people either for free
sold at such a massive discount
impossible that anyone on a $20 or $200-a-month plan could even afford
our_interpretation: Vast, vast majority means an overwhelming share of compute consumed, not merely a majority of users or accounts. No arbitrary percentage is imposed.
In context, the claim concerns compute serving AI applications, principally generative AI; whether training is included remains ambiguous.
Use April through June 2026, the latest completed quarter before publication that usage evidence could report on.
The affordability assertion concerns equivalent actual usage at unsubsidized cost, not the maximum theoretical subscription allowance.
API list prices are not assumed to equal providers' actual token costs.
This is an industry usage-share and household-affordability claim, not a stated financial metric for a particular company.
criteria.support_condition: Representative compute-weighted data show overwhelming use by free or deeply subsidized services, and usage, cost and financial-capacity data substantiate the subscriber affordability assertion.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative data show a substantial non-subsidized compute share inconsistent with overwhelming dominance, or documented subscribers can afford their equivalent usage at actual cost.
